```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

```{r}
library(simcompR)
```

A feedback cycle made only of direct-feedthrough blocks defines a signal
implicitly, $y = f(y, u)$, at every instant. Such a cycle is an
*algebraic loop*. A cycle that passes through an integrator, a delay or any
other block without direct feedthrough is ordinary dynamic feedback and is
not a loop.

## Detection

Compilation builds the graph of direct-feedthrough dependencies and finds
its strongly connected components. A component with more than one block,
or a block wired to itself, is a loop. By default it is an error, with one
cycle printed:

```{r, error = TRUE}
m <- sim_model("loop")
sim_add_block(m, "constant", "u", value = 1)
sim_add_block(m, "sum", "s", signs = "+-")
sim_add_block(m, "gain", "k", gain = 2)
sim_connect(m, "u", "s", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "k", "s", input = 2)
sim_connect(m, "s", "k")
sim_compile(m)
```

`simcompR` never breaks a loop by inserting a hidden delay: that would
change the mathematics silently.

## Solving loops

With `algebraic_loops = "solve"` each loop is solved at every evaluation.
The unknowns are the outputs $z$ of the blocks in the loop, and the
residual is $F(z) - z$, where $F$ evaluates the loop blocks once from the
guessed outputs. Newton's method with a finite-difference Jacobian and a
backtracking line search drives the residual below `loop_tol`.

```{r}
plan <- sim_compile(m, algebraic_loops = "solve")
plan
r <- sim_run(plan, c(0, 1), times = c(0, 1))
sim_signal(r, "s")   # s = 1 - 2 s, so 1/3
sim_diagnostics(r)$loop_residuals
```

The residual and iteration count at every recorded time are part of the
result diagnostics. A loop that does not converge is an error, never a
silently inconsistent result.

### A nonlinear loop

$y = \cos(y)$ has the unique solution $y \approx 0.739085$:

```{r}
nl <- sim_model("cos_loop")
sim_add_block(nl, "math", "c", fun = "cos")
sim_add_block(nl, "gain", "y", gain = 1)
sim_connect(nl, "c", "y")
sim_connect(nl, "y", "c")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(nl, algebraic_loops = "solve"), c(0, 1), times = 1)
sim_signal(r, "y")
```

### Loops without a solution

$y = y + 1$ has no solution. The Jacobian of the residual is singular and
the run fails with an explanation:

```{r, error = TRUE}
bad <- sim_model("inconsistent")
sim_add_block(bad, "constant", "one")
sim_add_block(bad, "sum", "s")
sim_connect(bad, "one", "s", input = 1)
sim_connect(bad, "s", "s", input = 2)
sim_run(sim_compile(bad, algebraic_loops = "solve"), c(0, 1))
```

### Several solutions and starting values

$y = 4 / y$ has the solutions $2$ and $-2$. Newton's method started from
zero cannot move (the residual is not even defined there), so the run
fails and says how to fix it. A starting value given with `loop_guess`
selects the solution:

```{r, error = TRUE}
two <- sim_model("two_roots")
sim_add_block(two, "constant", "four", value = 4)
sim_add_block(two, "divide", "y")
sim_connect(two, "four", "y", input = 1)
sim_connect(two, "y", "y", input = 2)
sim_run(sim_compile(two, algebraic_loops = "solve"), c(0, 1), times = 1)
pos <- sim_compile(two, algebraic_loops = "solve", loop_guess = list(y = 1))
neg <- sim_compile(two, algebraic_loops = "solve", loop_guess = list(y = -1))
c(sim_signal(sim_run(pos, c(0, 1), times = 1), "y"),
  sim_signal(sim_run(neg, c(0, 1), times = 1), "y"))
```

Every solve starts from the same value, so results never depend on the
history of the solver's trial points.

## Loops inside dynamics

Loops can sit inside a continuous model. Here
$\dot x = s$ with $s = -x - s$, so $\dot x = -x/2$:

```{r}
dyn <- sim_model("dynamic_loop")
sim_add_block(dyn, "integrator", "x", initial = 1)
sim_add_block(dyn, "sum", "s", signs = "--")
sim_add_block(dyn, "gain", "k", gain = 1)
sim_connect(dyn, "x", "s", input = 1)
sim_connect(dyn, "k", "s", input = 2)
sim_connect(dyn, "s", "k")
sim_connect(dyn, "s", "x")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(dyn, algebraic_loops = "solve"), c(0, 4),
             rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
max(abs(sim_signal(r, "x") - exp(-sim_times(r) / 2)))
```

Every derivative evaluation solves the loop, which costs extra function
evaluations. When possible, solve the loop by hand (here, replace the loop
by a gain of 1/2) or break it with a physically meaningful state.

## Feedthrough that depends on parameters

Whether a state-space block has direct feedthrough depends on its `D`
matrix. A plan whose `D` changes from zero to nonzero through
`sim_set_params()` is analyzed again, so a new loop is never missed. See
`vignette("compilation")`.

## Limits

* Loop solving uses a dense finite-difference Jacobian; it is meant for
  small loops.
* Switching blocks inside a loop take their mode from the solved signals
  at every segment boundary (repeated until the modes settle) and keep it
  inside the segment, where their crossing functions locate changes.
* Consistent initialization of differential-algebraic systems is not
  covered here; see the roadmap.
